title: Epochal journal quarantine and evict-resume runtime patch
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple production escalations across Hosted, Dedicated and Private clusters (customer tickets + Sev2 pager alerts) converged on a common failure mode: a latent journal replay path interacting with concurrent eviction that produced persistent KV tombstones and unreclaimed tensor arena allocations. The observable symptom was sudden GPU OOM windows on otherwise healthy nodes, often after transient load spikes or node restart. Impact: customer-facing latency spikes and failed requests; several enterprise tenants on Dedicated and Private reported repeat OOMs requiring node reboots or tenant isolation.
long_description: Root cause (short): During session recovery the journal replay routine could rehydrate entries into the KV index while the eviction controller was concurrently resuming in-flight eviction epochs. Race between the journal epoch replay writer and evictor led to orphaned KV handles and tombstone entries that prevented downstream compaction. Orphan handles kept small tensor arenas referenced, causing fragmentation and slow-but-steady growth of resident GPU memory until OOM. In Private deployments an interaction with our on-prem KMS rotation sequence occasionally extended recovery windows, increasing likelihood of the race. Why previous mitigations failed: simple eviction backoffs and aggressive GC made symptoms less frequent but did not fix the root asynchronous replay + eviction interlock.
proposed_fix: Introduce an epochal quarantine for journal replay: replayed entries land in a quarantined, single-writer staging area that is invisible to the eviction index until a commit gate validates checksums and monotonic epoch tokens. Evict-resume semantics are changed so that eviction preflight acquires a short-lived epoch token that prevents the replayer from promoting quarantined entries until eviction completes. The hotfix also adds a lightweight checksum on KV headers to detect and drop partial replays, and a targeted compaction task that reclaims tombstones and coalesces small arenas. The patch is implemented conservatively: config flag 'runtime.kv.quarantine=true' and 'runtime.kv.evict_epoch_timeout_ms=250' to allow rollback.
mitigations_for_customers: 1) Immediate: for affected customers we recommend tenant-level session capping (limit concurrent sessions per tenant) and temporary node cordon + graceful restart to clear fragmentation. 2) Near-term: enable runtime.kv.quarantine on canary pools to validate. 3) For Private installs we provide an upgrade bundle and an operator playbook to run the tombstone compactor and verify checksums before uncordon.
rollout_plan: - Stage 1: Deploy to internal canaries (5% of capacity) with telemetry turned on. Monitor GPU resident growth and kv-tombstone-rate for 24h. - Stage 2: Expand to low-risk hosted pools and two Dedicated clusters (25%). - Stage 3: Push to all Hosted and Dedicated, then offer Private upgrade package. Rollout window: 3 days with automatic rollback if OOM rate > 2x baseline or latency P99 regresses by >20% for 1h.
qa_and_tests: Unit tests for quarantine state transitions, integration tests that inject controlled replay+evict races, stress test harness reproducing fragmentation pattern at scale, and e2e smoke in canary environment. Add regression test to nightly suite to simulate KMS-induced recovery delays in Private.
monitoring_and_success_criteria: Primary metrics: gpu_oom_count (per-node), kv_tombstone_rate, resident_gpu_bytes, compaction_reclaims_per_minute, request_error_rate. Success = drop gpu_oom_count by >90% for impacted tenants and sustained resident memory stabilization within 24h of rollout. No customer-reported recurrence for 7 days.
rollback_plan: Flip runtime.kv.quarantine=false and revert evict_epoch_timeout to previous value; if immediate rollback required, cordon affected nodes and restart runtime process to clear quarantine staging area. Documented rollback commands included in runbook.
long_term_actions: 1) Replace ad-hoc journal with versioned checkpointing and atomic promotion path. 2) Improve KV telemetry: per-tenant handle counts and arena fragmentation histograms. 3) Harden Private upgrade sequence to avoid prolonged KMS pauses during critical recovery windows. 4) Postmortem to be completed within 7 days.
